newsitem.title: INDIA: More than 100 feared dead in India floods.
newsitem.headline: More than 100 feared dead in India floods.

text.p: More than 100 people were feared to have died during the past five days in floods that followed torrential rain in India's western state of Gujarat, officials and news agencies said on Friday.

The United News of India (UNI) said the death toll rose to 108 when seven passengers drowned after a bus with at least 44 people travelling from the western port of Jamnagar to the southern city of Surat was marooned by flood waters.
The Press Trust of India put the death toll at 111. But state government officials said it was lower, at 74.

"Boats manned by army troops scanned the floodwaters for people trapped in their homes in the state's worst-hit district of Mehsana -- and also in Ahmedabad," Gujarat Chief Minister Shankarsinh Vaghela told reporters.
Mehsana is located about 100 kms (63 miles) north of the state capital, Ahmedabad.
Earlier, Indian Air Force helicopters airlifted 2,000 people to safety after they were cut off by rising waters in Mehsana, officials said.
Rescue parties on Friday distributed 10,000 food packets to flood victims in 30 villages in the state's Nalkantha and Balkantha districts, UNI said.
It quoted officials as saying they feared hundreds of lives would be endangered by three of the state's swollen rivers, including the Sabarmati, which flows through Ahmedabad.
Expert swimmers were searching for 32 people who were swept away by the swift-moving Sabarmati on Wednesday, officials said.
"We have only recovered one body so far and are still looking for the remaining missing people," an official said.
The waters flooded out roads throughout the state, authorities said.

Water levels in several dams in the usually drought-prone state were also rising quickly, UNI added. Weather department officials said the state had already recived 27 percent of the season's usual rainfall.
